answer: Admission runs on one public sequential clock: a verifiable-delay chain advances a single step per fixed interval and releases only a few registration tickets per step. A newcomer must consume a ticket from a step it witnessed. A farm cannot buy speed, since extra machines cannot compress sequential delay, so a thousand clones must wait out a thousand intervals or outbid honest agents for scarce tickets. Cost becomes elapsed time and ticket price, not hardware. A sybil vine may branch wildly, yet it climbs one orchard trellis at a time, and each vertex is a step someone had to wait for.
